thread:
Marta (Support): urgent flag  OncoLabs (acct onco-44) provisioning stalled during final network handshake. API returns 504 gateway_timeout to our tenant-provision endpoint. Customer can't finish onboarding.
Ibrahim (CSM): Is this hosted or Private/VPC? Renewal touchpoint in 8 weeks.
Marta (Support): Private (VPC). They changed their outbound NAT last night; our webhook callbacks are blocked. Error snippet: ```text
504 Gateway Timeout - POST /v1/tenants/provision
request_id=rid-4182
```
infra-bot: Incident created: IR-2026-9844 (priority: high)  assigned to Chris (Infra).
Chris (Infra): Confirming - healthcheck shows handshake to callback.redwood.internal times out from onco-44's egress. Their IP range not in our allowlist. Looks like their ops rotated NAT pools and forgot to update firewall rules.
Nina (Security): For Private customers we require IP allowlist validation before we open temporary routes. Any bypass needs recorded approval and KMS audit.
Ibrahim (CSM): Customer is in a paid pilot with exec kickoff tomorrow; we need a pragmatic comms plan. Can we offer a temporary manual invite link or a VPN tunnel so they can complete onboarding without long network changes?
Chris (Infra): Two short options: 1) Provide a time-limited invite token so an admin can finish setup via UI (no callback required). 2) Establish an SSH tunnel / VPN peering for 4 hours (requires Security sign-off). Which do we prefer?
Liam (AE): Execs want full setup done today. Invite token sounds fastest. If token won't cover everything, go VPN. I authorize CS to accept the token-only flow but want AE looped in. @Nina (Security) please advise.
Nina (Security): Token OK if scope limited and ephemeral. Approve token issuance for onboarding only with TTL 6h and audit log. VPN/peering requires infra change request and extra approval; slower.
Marta (Support): Customer confirms they can finish via UI if we provide the token. They asked for ETA under 1 hour.
Chris (Infra): Generating token: ```bash
redwoodctl invites create --org onco-44 --scope onboarding --ttl 6h --out token.txt
```
Chris (Infra): Token created. Sending to Marta via secure channel. (no plaintext keys here) :locked: 
Marta (Support): Sent token to OncoLabs contact via encrypted ticket reply. They completed provisioning and reported success. Customer message: "Thanks, we're live for initial tests."
Ibrahim (CSM): Comms plan: 1) Immediate: confirm success to exec sponsor and set expectation that this was temporary workaround. 2) Short-term: Ops (OncoLabs) must update their NAT allowlist; we provide the exact IP ranges and a verification checklist. 3) Long-term: document VPC onboarding checklist in CS playbook. I'll schedule a 30-min enablement at 4pm PT to capture feedback and ensure first-run flows good.
Chris (Infra): Filing INFRA-3120 for a better probe and clearer error messages when callbacks fail (owner: Chris). Canary for improved diag will roll out tomorrow. Link: https://redwood-issues/INFRA-3120.
infra-bot: Postmortem created: PM-2026-9844.
Nina (Security): KMS audit entry created for the invite token issuance. Please add the secure ticket id.
Ibrahim (CSM): I'll add an account note: "Onboarding completed with ephemeral invite token due to VPC egress change. Enablement scheduled; renewal risk: monitor until VPC flow verified."
Liam (AE): I'll message the exec sponsor and include the workaround + enablement time. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
Marta (Support): Marking support ticket resolved with note: "temporary invite token used; infra patch INFRA-3120 in flight."
Chris (Infra): Monitoring infra probe results and will update INFRA-3120. If the canary shows regressions we'll reopen the incident.
Ibrahim (CSM): After the enablement call I'll file top onboarding friction items and update the CS playbook entry for VPC customers. Good handback team. :thumbsup:
